mappings.rationale: The ISMP requirement is an ISMS-establishment obligation; 5.1 covers the documented, management-approved policy set that constitutes it and 5.35 covers the Level 3 requirement for independent audits of the program's continuing suitability, but the PDCA management-system framing itself sits in ISO 27001 rather than 27002.
Both require a documented access control policy established and reviewed on the basis of business and information security requirements.
Formal user registration/de-registration is exactly 5.16's full identity life cycle, and the granting and revoking of access it drives is 5.18's provisioning and removal of access rights.
Restricting and controlling the allocation and use of privileges is the literal subject of 8.2 Privileged Access Rights.
Formal management process for issuing, distributing and revoking passwords is 5.17's allocation and management of authentication information.
User obligations for password selection and secrecy are the user-responsibility half of 5.17, and making users aware of those obligations is delivered through 6.3 awareness training.
Protecting unattended equipment (session lock, log-off, screen lock) is the clear-screen half of 7.7, applied to the endpoints 8.1 governs.
Same control on both sides: a clear desk policy for papers and removable media plus a clear screen policy for information processing facilities.
Strong/multi-factor authentication for remote users is 8.5 Secure Authentication, and the remote-connection context it protects is 6.7 Remote Working.

Automatic equipment identification authenticates a device rather than a person; ISO 27002:2022 dropped the standalone 2005 control and now treats device identities inside 5.16's identity life cycle, so the overlap is real but partial.

Controlling physical and logical access to diagnostic and configuration ports is handled in 27002:2022 as network port hardening under 8.20 and as enforced secure configuration (disabling unused ports/services) under 8.9; there is no dedicated diagnostic-port clause.
Segregating groups of information services, users and systems onto separate networks is precisely 8.22 Segregation of Networks.
Restricting users' ability to connect on shared and boundary-crossing networks is enforced by 8.20 network security controls, in line with the access control policy of 5.15.
Routing controls that stop information flows breaching application access policy were folded into 8.20 Networks Security in the 2022 revision; no separate routing-control clause survives.
Providing users only the network services they are specifically authorized to use is the authorization requirement of 8.21, exercised through the access control policy in 5.15.
Secure log-on procedures (limited feedback, failed-attempt handling, no system detail before authentication) are the substance of 8.5 Secure Authentication.
A unique user ID per person is 5.16's identity uniqueness requirement, and substantiating the claimed identity by an authentication technique is 8.5.
An interactive password management system enforcing quality passwords is 5.17 (authentication information management) implemented through 8.5's secure authentication system requirements.
Restricting utility programs capable of overriding system and application controls is verbatim 8.18 Use of Privileged Utility Programs.
Terminating inactive sessions after a defined period is guidance inside 8.5 Secure Authentication; ISO 27002:2022 has no standalone session time-out control.
Connection-time windows for high-risk applications survive in 27002:2022 only as an example restriction under 8.5/5.15; the dedicated 2005 control was retired, so this is a thematic link only.
Restricting access to information and application system functions per the access control policy is exactly 8.3 Information Access Restriction.
A dedicated isolated computing environment for sensitive systems is network/system isolation under 8.22, and designing that isolation into the system is 8.27's secure architecture principles.
A policy and protective measures for mobile computing and communication devices is 8.1 User Endpoint Devices, with 6.7 covering the off-premises use context.
Teleworking policy, plans and procedures are the entire subject of 6.7 Remote Working.
Defining and documenting security roles and responsibilities for staff and third-party users is 5.2, and embedding them in the employment relationship is 6.2.
Background verification of candidates, contractors and third-party users proportional to business requirements is verbatim 6.1 Screening.
Signed employment terms stating information security responsibilities is exactly 6.2 Terms and Conditions of Employment.
Management requiring personnel to apply security per established policies and procedures is verbatim 5.4 Management Responsibilities.
Awareness training and regular policy updates for employees, contractors and third-party users relevant to job function is verbatim 6.3.
A formal disciplinary process for security policy violations is verbatim 6.4 Disciplinary Process.
Defining and assigning responsibilities for termination or change of employment is 6.5 Responsibilities After Termination or Change of Employment.
Return of all organizational assets on termination of employment, contract or agreement is verbatim 5.11 Return of Assets.
Removal on termination and adjustment on role change of access rights is the revocation half of 5.18 Access Rights.

Establishing and maintaining a risk management program is an ISMS management-system requirement (ISO 27001 clause 6.1) — ISO 27002:2022 is a control catalogue and contains no risk-management-program control, so mapping it anywhere would be a fabrication.

Performing risk assessments to identify and quantify risk corresponds to ISO 27001 clauses 6.1.2 and 8.2, not to any control in the ISO 27002:2022 catalogue; 8.8 covers only technical-vulnerability evaluation, which is a narrower and different activity.

Risk mitigation/treatment to an acceptable level is ISO 27001 clause 6.1.3 (risk treatment plan and Statement of Applicability); ISO 27002:2022 supplies the treatment options but has no control that requires the treatment decision itself.
Continual re-evaluation and reassessment of risk is ISO 27001 clauses 8.2 and 9.3 (periodic risk assessment and management review); no ISO 27002:2022 control expresses this obligation.
Management-approved, published and communicated information security policy documents are verbatim the first half of 5.1 Policies for Information Security.
Review of the security policy at planned intervals or on significant change is verbatim the second half of 5.1.
Active management support through clear direction and explicit assignment of security responsibilities is 5.4, expressed through the approved policy framework of 5.1.
Coordination of security activities by representatives from different parts of the organization is the cross-functional role-allocation requirement inside 5.2.
Clear definition of all information security responsibilities is verbatim 5.2 Information Security Roles and Responsibilities.

A management authorization process before new information assets and facilities enter service maps to 5.8's requirement to address security when introducing new systems, with the resulting asset recorded under 5.9; ISO 27002:2022 retired the standalone 2005 authorization control.
Identifying and regularly reviewing confidentiality/non-disclosure agreement requirements is verbatim 6.6.
Maintaining appropriate contacts with relevant authorities is verbatim 5.5 Contact with Authorities.
Maintaining contacts with special interest groups and specialist security forums is verbatim 5.6.
Independent review of the security approach, control objectives, policies and processes at planned intervals is verbatim 5.35 Independent Review of Information Security.
Identifying risks from business processes involving external parties and implementing controls before granting access is the core of 5.19 Information Security in Supplier Relationships.

ISO 27002:2022 has no customer-specific clause; addressing security requirements before customers access information maps to the agreement-terms requirement of 5.20 and the authorization requirement of 5.15.
Requiring third-party agreements to cover all relevant security requirements is verbatim 5.20, with 5.21 covering the ICT product/service supply-chain terms the control extends to.
Explicitly defining, documenting and keeping current all statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements per system is verbatim 5.31.
Procedures ensuring compliance with IPR legislation and proprietary software licence terms is verbatim 5.32 Intellectual Property Rights.
Protecting important records from loss, destruction and falsification per statutory and business retention requirements is verbatim 5.33 Protection of Records.
Ensuring data protection and privacy of covered information as required by legislation is verbatim 5.34 Privacy and Protection of PII.
Deterring users from using information assets for unauthorized purposes is the acceptable-use and misuse-deterrence requirement of 5.10.

Use of cryptographic controls in compliance with agreements, laws and regulations combines 8.24's cryptography rules with 5.31's legal-requirement identification (export/import and key-escrow law); neither clause alone carries the crypto-regulation angle.
Managers verifying that security procedures in their area achieve compliance with policies and standards is verbatim 5.36 Compliance with Policies, Rules and Standards.
Regular technical compliance checking of systems against security implementation standards is the technical-review half of 5.36, executed through the scanning and testing activity described in 8.8.
Planning and agreeing audit activities on operational systems to minimize business disruption is verbatim 8.34 Protection of Information Systems During Audit Testing.
Protecting access to audit tools to prevent misuse or compromise is the audit-tool safeguarding requirement inside 8.34.
Identifying all assets and drawing up and maintaining an inventory is verbatim 5.9 Inventory of Information and Other Associated Assets.
Assigning a designated owner to every information asset is the ownership requirement folded into 5.9 in the 2022 revision.
Identifying, documenting and implementing rules for acceptable use of information and associated assets is verbatim 5.10.
Classifying information by value, legal requirements, sensitivity and criticality is verbatim 5.12 Classification of Information.
Procedures for information labelling in line with the adopted classification scheme is verbatim 5.13; the handling half of the control is covered by 5.10.
Using security perimeters (walls, controlled entry gates, manned reception) to protect areas containing information assets is verbatim 7.1.
Protecting secure areas by entry controls so only authorized personnel gain access is verbatim 7.2 Physical Entry.
Designing and applying physical security for offices, rooms and facilities is verbatim 7.3.
Physical protection against fire, flood, earthquake, explosion, civil unrest and other natural or man-made disasters is verbatim 7.5.
Physical protection and guidelines for working in secure areas is verbatim 7.6.

ISO 27002:2022 merged the 2005 delivery-and-loading-area control into 7.2 Physical Entry, whose guidance explicitly covers isolating delivery areas from information processing facilities, with the perimeter itself under 7.1.
Siting or protecting equipment to reduce environmental risk and unauthorized-access opportunity is verbatim 7.8 Equipment Siting and Protection.
Protecting equipment from power failures and other supporting-utility disruptions is verbatim 7.11 Supporting Utilities.
Protecting power and telecommunications cabling from interception or damage is verbatim 7.12 Cabling Security.
Correct maintenance of equipment to ensure continued availability and integrity is verbatim 7.13 Equipment Maintenance.
Applying security to off-site equipment accounting for the risks of working outside the premises is verbatim 7.9 Security of Assets Off-Premises.
Verifying that covered information and licensed software is removed or securely overwritten before disposal or re-use is verbatim 7.14, applied to the storage media governed by 7.10.
ISO 27002:2022 merged the 2005 removal-of-assets control into 7.9, whose guidance requires prior authorization before equipment, information or software is taken off site.
Documented, maintained operating procedures made available to those who need them is verbatim 5.37 Documented Operating Procedures.
Controlling and archiving changes to information assets and processing systems is verbatim 8.32 Change Management.
Enforcing separation of duties to reduce opportunity for unauthorized or unintentional modification or misuse is verbatim 5.3 Segregation of Duties.
Separating and controlling development, test and operational environments is verbatim 8.31.

Ensuring the third party actually implements, operates and maintains the controls, service definitions and delivery levels in the agreement is the delivery-assurance half of 5.22, against the terms set in 5.20.
Regular monitoring, review and audit of third-party services, reports and records is verbatim the monitoring and review half of 5.22.
Managing changes to third-party service provision weighing business criticality is verbatim the change-management half of 5.22, aligned with the organization's own change control in 8.32.
Planning and managing adequate capacity and resources to deliver required system performance is verbatim 8.6 Capacity Management.

Establishing acceptance criteria and testing systems, upgrades and new versions before acceptance is verbatim 8.29 Security Testing in Development and Acceptance, with the criteria themselves drawn from 8.26.
Detection, prevention and recovery controls against malicious code plus user awareness is verbatim 8.7 Protection Against Malware.

ISO 27002:2022 retired the standalone mobile-code control and absorbed it into 8.7's malware guidance; authorizing mobile code before installation and use also overlaps 8.19's control over what software may run on operational systems.
Taking and regularly testing back-up copies of information and software is verbatim 8.13 Information Backup.
Managing and controlling networks to protect systems and applications including information in transit is verbatim 8.20 Networks Security.
Identifying security features, service levels and management requirements of network services and including them in the network services agreement, in-house or outsourced, is verbatim 8.21.
Documented formal procedures for managing removable media is the acquisition-to-disposal life cycle in 7.10 Storage Media.
Secure disposal of media no longer required by documented formal procedures is the disposal requirement of 7.10, with 8.10 covering the deletion of the information the media holds.

ISO 27002:2022 folded the 2005 handling-of-assets control into 5.10; procedures for handling and storing information to prevent disclosure or misuse follow the classification and labelling scheme of 5.13, but no dedicated handling-procedures clause survives.

ISO 27002:2022 dropped the standalone system-documentation control; protecting system documentation from unauthorized access is now an instance of 8.3's restriction of access to information per the access control policy.
Formal exchange policies, procedures and controls protecting information transferred over all communication mediums is verbatim 5.14 Information Transfer.
Agreements for the exchange of information and software with external parties is the transfer-agreements requirement explicitly inside 5.14.
Protecting media in physical transit beyond organizational boundaries is the physical-media transfer requirement of 5.14, applied to the media governed by 7.10.
Protecting information involved in electronic messaging is the electronic-transfer requirement explicitly inside 5.14.

ISO 27002:2022 retired the 2005 interconnected-business-systems control; protecting information shared across interconnected systems now falls under 5.14's transfer rules and 8.20's controls on the connections carrying it.

ISO 27002:2022 folded electronic-commerce controls into 8.26, whose guidance explicitly addresses transaction protection over public networks against fraud, dispute and unauthorized disclosure, backed by the cryptography of 8.24.

8.26 explicitly requires application security requirements covering incomplete transmission, mis-routing, unauthorized message alteration, duplication and replay in transactional services — the same list this control states.

ISO 27002:2022 absorbed the 2005 publicly-available-information control into 8.26's application security requirements for publicly accessible systems; integrity of published information is an availability/integrity requirement there rather than its own clause.
Producing and retaining audit logs of user activities, exceptions and security events for future investigation is verbatim 8.15 Logging.
Procedures for monitoring use of information processing systems to check control use and effectiveness is verbatim 8.16 Monitoring Activities.
Protecting logging facilities and log information against tampering and unauthorized access is an explicit requirement inside 8.15.

Logging and regularly reviewing system administrator and operator activity is the privileged-user logging requirement of 8.15, and reviewing it is part of the oversight 8.2 demands for privileged access.
Fault logging survives in 27002:2022 as fault/error log content under 8.15 and as the anomaly analysis and remediation trigger under 8.16; there is no standalone fault-logging clause.
Synchronizing clocks of all relevant systems to an agreed accurate time source to support event correlation is verbatim 8.17 Clock Synchronization.

Specifying security control requirements in the business requirements for new or enhanced systems, whether developed or purchased, is verbatim 8.26, positioned at the requirements stage of the 8.25 life cycle.
Validating data input to applications and databases is an explicit application security requirement under 8.26 and an input-validation secure coding practice under 8.28.

Validation checks detecting corruption from processing errors or deliberate acts are internal-processing integrity checks — 27002:2022 covers them as secure coding practice (8.28) and as an application integrity requirement (8.26) rather than a dedicated clause.

Message authenticity and integrity is achieved through the cryptographic mechanisms of 8.24 (MACs, digital signatures) specified as an application requirement under 8.26; ISO 27002:2022 has no standalone message-integrity control.

Output validation to confirm processing of stored information is correct is an application security requirement under 8.26 and an output-handling secure coding practice under 8.28; the 2005 standalone control was retired.
A documented policy on the use of cryptographic controls supported by formal procedures is verbatim the policy requirement of 8.24 Use of Cryptography.
Key management supporting the organization's use of cryptographic techniques is the key life-cycle requirement explicitly inside 8.24.
Procedures controlling the installation of software on operational systems is verbatim 8.19 Installation of Software on Operational Systems.
Careful selection, protection and control of test data in non-production environments is verbatim 8.33 Test Information.
Restricting access to program source code is verbatim 8.4 Access to Source Code.
Formal change control procedures governing implementation of changes, patches, service packs and updates is verbatim 8.32 Change Management.
Supervising and monitoring outsourced software development is verbatim 8.30 Outsourced Development.
Obtaining timely technical vulnerability information, evaluating exposure and taking measures to address the risk is verbatim 8.8 Management of Technical Vulnerabilities.
Reporting information security events through appropriate channels as quickly as possible is verbatim 6.8 Information Security Event Reporting.
ISO 27002:2022 merged the 2005 security-weakness reporting control into 6.8, which requires personnel to report observed or suspected weaknesses as well as events.

Establishing management responsibilities and procedures for quick, effective and orderly incident response is verbatim 5.24 Incident Management Planning and Preparation, executed through 5.26 Response to Incidents.
Mechanisms to quantify and monitor the types, volumes and costs of incidents so lessons feed back into controls is verbatim 5.27 Learning from Information Security Incidents.
Collecting, retaining and presenting evidence admissible in civil or criminal proceedings after an incident is verbatim 5.28 Collection of Evidence.

A managed program and process for business continuity that addresses information security requirements is verbatim 5.29 Information Security During Disruption, with 5.30 covering its ICT readiness component.

Identifying interruption events with probability, impact and information security consequences is the business impact analysis that feeds 5.29's continuity planning and 5.30's RTO/RPO derivation; ISO 27002 states the planning obligation but not the BIA as its own control.

Developing and implementing plans to maintain or restore operations and information availability at required levels and timescales after failure is verbatim 5.29 and the ICT-recovery capability of 5.30.
A single consistent framework of continuity plans that addresses information security requirements and sets testing and maintenance priorities is the planning-structure requirement of 5.29.
Testing and updating continuity plans at least annually to confirm they remain current and effective is the exercise-and-review requirement stated in both 5.29 and 5.30.

Providing data subjects notice of uses and disclosures of their PII and of controller duties is a core PII-protection obligation, which 5.34 requires the organization to identify and meet under applicable privacy legislation.

Openness about PII-handling policies and practices is a privacy principle that 5.34 requires be satisfied per applicable law, but 27002:2022 delegates the substantive transparency requirements to ISO 27701 rather than stating them.

Recording disclosures of PII to third parties is a privacy-accountability obligation under 5.34, operationalized through the logging capability of 8.15; ISO 27002 has no disclosure-accounting control of its own.

Obtaining meaningful, informed, freely given consent is a lawful-basis requirement that 5.34 pulls in by reference to applicable privacy legislation, without ISO 27002 specifying the consent mechanics.
Offering data subjects choice to refuse, withdraw consent or object to processing is a data-subject-rights obligation covered only by 5.34's general requirement to meet applicable PII legislation.
Data subject access to review and challenge accuracy of their PII is a statutory access right that 5.34 requires be identified and satisfied; no other ISO 27002 clause addresses subject access.

Ensuring processing purposes comply with law and rest on a permissible legal ground is 5.34's PII-legislation compliance requirement, backed by 5.31's obligation to identify applicable legal requirements.

Specifying collection purposes at or before collection and limiting subsequent use is a privacy principle 5.34 incorporates by reference to applicable legislation, not an infosec control ISO 27002 defines.
Limiting PII collection to what law permits and the specified purpose strictly requires is a collection-limitation principle covered only through 5.34's general PII-protection obligation.

Minimizing PII processed and limiting disclosure to the fewest parties is a 5.34 privacy obligation; 8.11 provides the technical means (masking, pseudonymization) ISO 27002 offers for reducing exposed PII.
Limiting use and disclosure of PII to specific explicit legitimate purposes is a use-limitation principle that ISO 27002 addresses only through 5.34's requirement to comply with applicable PII law.
Retaining PII no longer than necessary combines 5.34's privacy obligation with 5.33's retention-schedule requirement for records and 8.10's requirement to delete information when no longer required.

Ensuring PII is accurate, complete, up-to-date, adequate and relevant is a data-quality obligation from privacy law (GDPR Art. 5(1)(d)); ISO 27002:2022 protects information integrity against unauthorized modification but contains no control requiring the substantive correctness of data content, so any mapping would misstate the requirement.

Propagating amendments, corrections and removals to processors and third-party recipients is a data-subject-redress obligation with no ISO 27002 analogue beyond 5.34's blanket requirement to meet applicable PII legislation.

Internal complaint handling and redress procedures for data subjects is a privacy-law process obligation (a customer-facing grievance mechanism); ISO 27002:2022 contains no complaint-management control, and 5.34 is a pointer to ISO 27701 rather than a substantive match, so an empty mapping is the honest result.

Establishing governance for PII processing means assigning a privacy function and accountability, which maps to 5.2's definition of security roles and responsibilities applied to the PII duties 5.34 requires.

Establishing and performing privacy impact assessments is a PII-specific obligation ISO 27002 covers only through 5.34's requirement to identify and meet applicable privacy legislation; the general risk-assessment process sits in ISO 27001, not 27002.

Contractually requiring third-party recipients to provide equivalent PII protection is exactly 5.20's requirement to address information security in supplier agreements, applied to the PII duties of 5.34.
Monitoring and auditing PII protection controls and internal policy effectiveness is 5.36's compliance-verification activity scoped to the privacy policy set that 5.34 requires.
Providing training and awareness on PII protection to personnel with access to PII is 6.3's awareness and training control with privacy as the subject matter required by 5.34.

Developing, disseminating and updating PII protection reports is an accountability/reporting duty to management and regulators; ISO 27002:2022 has no equivalent reporting control, so only 5.34's general privacy-compliance obligation relates, and weakly.
